title: heterogeneous-attention-fusion-with-staged-scheduler-and-continuous-batching-support
author: Maya Singh
description: Motivation: reduce p99 latency regression for mixed-sequence workloads and improve throughput for production chat and retrieval runtimes by selecting optimal attention kernels at runtime and enabling continuous batching without sacrificing KV cache hit stability. Changes: Introduces a heterogeneous attention selection layer (HeteroAttn) that picks between a low-latency microkernel and a high-throughput Flash-like kernel based on sequence length heuristics and current queueing pressure; adds a staged scheduler that enforces a short-term reservation window for latency-sensitive requests and a batch-aggregation window for throughput requests; implements a cooperative KV cache eviction policy (staged LRU) that works with continuous batching to avoid repeated cache thrash during rollups; adds fused rotary/rope offset precomputation paths that avoid memcpy for common rotary patterns; integrates fp16 accumulation path with optional fp32 fallback for edge-case stability; exposes runtime knobs: ATTEN_SELECT_WINDOW_MS, KV_STAGED_WINDOW, CBATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS for tuned rollouts. Testing and validation: microbenchmarked on c6i-gpu clusters and internal perf-lab; added synthetic mixed-sequence workload harness and end-to-end chat replay traces. Results: median latency improved 6-9% on mid-sized seqs, p99 reduced up to 22% for mixed workloads, throughput increased 12% on long-sequence tails while KV miss rate decreased 18% under continuous batching. Rollout plan: staged canary on dedicated pool alpha -> 50% traffic after 72h, automatic rollback on p99 regressions >10% or error rate increase >0.5%. Backwards compatibility: no API changes. Known limitations: rare fp16 accumulation differences at extreme sequence lengths (documented and guarded by runtime flag), scheduler parameters tuned for our standard clusters; customers on small on-prem may require adjustments. Checklist: - [x] Benchmarks added to perf-lab harness - [x] Unit + integration tests for scheduler and KV policy - [x] Feature-flagged rollout - [x] Docs entry in runtime tuning guide - [x] Telemetry events for selection decisions

review_comments: Ethan Park: Overall this looks good; two questions: 1) how stable is the fp16 accumulation path on long sequences? 2) we need a clearer metric in telemetry for selection reversions.

Maya Singh (author): FP16 path has guard to fall back to fp32 when accumulation overflow detected; unit test added for 32k token synthetic to assert no NaNs. Added selection_reversion_count metric and exposed in selection_events.
Sofia Ramirez: Could you add a small note in the docs about recommended KV_STAGED_WINDOW for Dedicated vs Hosted? Length of default felt tuned for large pools.
Maya Singh: Added docs entry and example per-cluster recommendation; default remains conservative and can be overridden per deployment.
Liam O'Connor: CI flake on cuda11.8 matrix, reran and passed; good to squash merge once e2e looks green.
release_notes: Introduces heterogeneous attention kernel selection with staged scheduler and continuous batching support. Improves p99 and throughput for mixed-sequence workloads. Feature-flagged; not a public API change. See docs/runtime/tuning/hetero_attn.md for tuning guidance.
